inputs.original_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has granted regular bail to a man accused under national security provisions and the Official Secrets Act on the grounds that mere suspicion of sharing sensitive information with a contact in Pakistan is not enough to justify keeping him locked up. He was allegedly in telephonic contact with a Karachi-based "Punjabi Kuri." This decision puts the rights of the accused ahead of real threats to our borders and sovereignty. Our courts keep favoring individual freedom over the basic duty to protect the nation, its traditions, and its security. This activist approach only weakens authority and invites further erosion of the order that keeps our country safe.
inputs.modified_text: The Punjab and Haryana High Court has handed regular bail to a man accused under national security provisions and the Official Secrets Act, claiming mere suspicion of sharing sensitive information with a contact in Pakistan is not enough to keep him locked up. He was allegedly in telephonic contact with a Karachi-based "Punjabi Kuri." This is another case of the courts elevating the rights of the accused over the clear dangers to our borders and sovereignty. They keep choosing individual freedom instead of the duty to safeguard the nation, its traditions, and its security. This activist mindset only erodes the authority and order essential to protecting us from outside threats.
